title: Nell and the Old Shell
checkpoint: Reception Summer 1, week 4 — Phase 4: Two-syllable words: longer words with two syllables (no new sounds)
note_for_grown_ups: Non-fiction, Phase 4, 63-sound stage (pr, sc, sk just added). A true fact: empty shells found in the garden often belonged to a snail or similar small creature that has since moved on or been eaten.

pages.illustration: Nell the bee flying low over a vegetable patch full of leafy plants.
Nell spotting a round pale brown shell lying among the vegetable leaves.
Nell the bee landing gently on top of the round shell.
Nell the bee tapping the shell with one leg.
Close view of the still, quiet shell, nothing coming out of it.
Nell the bee peering closely into the open end of the shell.

pages.text: The shell has no bug in it.
pages.illustration: Close view inside the shell, showing it empty and a little worn.
A small grey slug resting on a leaf near the empty shell, a similar creature to whatever once lived inside it.

pages.text: Nell flaps on. The shell sits in the plot.
pages.illustration: Nell the bee flying off, leaving the empty shell resting among the vegetable leaves.
